title: Just so helpful!
body:
I use this app on a near daily basis. I have the type of personality that likes to tick off the things I have done and this gives me that; but, more than that, it really helps me organise my days and various events. In this way, I can quietly think through all the elements of a task, order them, and then check them off as I am moving to completion.

As an older person, I appreciate being able to externalise the things I need to do, as it helps me retain a sense of control over household and other matters.

I also have left some tasks as permanent lists - like ‘packing to go away’ - and since doing that, I have never left a phone cable or toothbrush behind!

I highly recommend this app - easy to use, and just so helpful.

More support with google calendar and notes would be appreciated, as tasks don’t seem to sync with the Calender.. 

All in all, I know Tasks is somewhat primitive compared to other to-do apps, but is the only app that doesn’t force a subscription for excessive usage and plus, is constantly being updated, I can only hope for the best.

title: Finally!
body:
I use a lot of Goole tools, including tasks as it has an unobtrusive integration with my email workflow.

My greatest complaint has been that the Tasks functionality has never ventured beyond the desktop.

Finally my todo lists can integrate with my phone cleanly. 

I know that Keep does a lot of this and the new ‘Inbox” tries to do tasks as well, but there is an elegant simplicity in just having a list of tasks. 

For a lot of folks, like myself, don’t need or want a lot of bells and whistles - we just need a list that syncs with our desktops. 

This is it. Simplicity itself. 

My only ask to make it better would be to allow the Gmail app to be able to assign a task from an email. Just like on the desktop. That would make this perfect for all time. If you had that, I’d have given 5-stars.

It feels like there are 50 different ways you can create tasks and reminders in Google's ecosystem, none of them talk to each other. Google just needs a simple way to take notes (Keep is great) and a simple way to make tasks with reminders that are accessible from Gmail and Calendar - hopefully this app will be the answer to this conundrum.

title: Not able to set up my own order
body:

For me, it’s very important to have tasks in a specific order, since I use them as side work and need to follow them step by step. It would be extremely helpful if the app allowed me to set and lock a custom order for my tasks, so they stay exactly as I arrange them.
Thank you for considering this feature — it would make the app much more effective for people who need structured workflows.

title: Widget
body: Widget do aplicativo desaparece e reaparece aleatoriamente. Não me refiro a quando o celular está bloqueado, quando o conteúdo do widget está ocultado, mas a quando o celular está bloqueado ou desbloqueado e o widget literalmente some. Outra coisa é que, pra mim, um ponto negativo claro do design do widget é o de que, mesmo com o widget mais largo, dificilmente você poderá ler o texto completo de uma tarefa nele, e, na maioria das vezes, só conseguirá ler um trecho muito pequeno. Acredito que isso poderia ser facilmente melhorado movendo o nome da lista e o botão para adicionar uma nova tarefa, que estão na parte esquerda do widget mais largo, para a o topo, liberando mais espaço para o texto das tarefas. Ademais, acredito que, para a liberação de um espaço ainda maior para o texto das tarefas, a data das tarefas também poderia ser movida para o topo. Dessa forma, ao invés de sempre ter a data disposta ao final de todas as tarefas, repetindo uma mesma data quando há várias tarefas marcadas para aquele dia, o widget poderia ser dividido entre partes que agrupassem as tarefas de uma mesma data, ou as tarefas que não tem uma data especificada, com as tarefas marcadas para o dia 17/07, como por exemplo, listadas abaixo desta data. O único porém disso seria a redução do espaço vertical para a exibição de um maior número de tarefas no widget. Para mim, a solução disso seria a criação de um widget maior, um quadrado que ocupa um espaço equivalente a aproximadamente dois do widget retangular e quatro do widget do quadrado pequeno, que é uma opção de widget que existe para diversos outros aplicativos. Dessa forma, existiria uma opção para aqueles que quisessem uma menor subtração do texto de suas tarefas no widget.

Falta uma versão pra iPad e também a possibilidade de compartilhar listas. O visual é muito bom. Limpo e polido. A usabilidade também é elogiável.

title: Please add these features
body:
1. Export task list to textable/emailable/ doc format
2. Please allow a task created in the main list to be assigned to a space, not to need to create the task within spaces. Furthermore, create the ability to move a task from one space to another, or to populate multiple spaces.
3. Add Subtask feature to tasks within spaces as well, just as it does in the main task list.
4. Allow to create task templates for repeated work flows,  both in main task and within spaces.
5. Integrate tasks with google sheets. Allow a spreadsheet field to convert to a linkable task, by right clicking. Furthermore, allow an entire task list template to create a spreadsheet (with gantt template would be awesome). Allow the task template to populate the spreadsheet with the whole templated task list.  This would allow for pipeline work flows that are repateable and easily created. 

Overall, a good app, but with the amazing new spaces, and the robust google sheets, the lack of integration is stoping the task feature from being 5 stars.

title: Not giving notifications and not persistent notifications.
body:
I really want to like and use this app. I deleted it a few months ago due to not being able to add repeating tasks or assign a time to a task. Now you add both of those. I test it and some tasks just aren’t popping notifications. I believe it might be due to do not disturb mode but will do more testing. I had multiple tasks set this morning just as a test. Do not disturb set to end at 7am. 2 tasks set to trigger at 7am. Nothing happened and nothing in the notification pull down menu. Useless! Yes I have iOS set to give me notifications for this app. All options are enabled. 

I also recall last version the notifications would not persist. Like you hear the ding. Then pull down the menu to look see it. Turn off the phone screen and turn it on again and it’s gone. Again, useless! Have completed the task yet and still need to see the reminder!

I’m kind of mad now that yesterday I deleted all my tasks from iOS reminders app when I installed this latest version due to the new features I wanted. Now I want to go back...iOS reminders app is flawless and the reminders are persistent in the drop down menu.

title: What is the point?
body:
“One of the world’s richest companies writing one of the least capable apps.”  That should be the tag line.

We use Google’s tasks throughout our day, every day.  We use both the web version and the service through through GoTasks (which I, unfortunately, no longer see on the AppStore).

The web version is simple and works well.  This version has been out for how long?  It only now supports the iPad, and it still doesn’t support the basic functionality of Google’s web version. Where are the sub items, never mind the other basic service features.  It’s support for sub items is to flatten my list?  When I add a new item, sometimes the text area shows up so I can see what I’m typing, aaaand sometimes it doesn’t.

I could go on, but what’s the point?  It’s simpler to abandon this app and find something that isn’t a joke.  After all, given the ridiculously minimal amount of attention Google has given it, aren’t they simply going to abandon it, too?  After all, it’s what they do!

Google:  look at GoTasks, if you can find it. It’s so much simpler and elegant, and, yet, so much more capable...with your own service!

title: This app so lean I shouldn’t have to list for free
body:
This is the leanest to do app you’re gonna ever get.

It’s actually more like a sheet of paper, but on your phone. Out of the box you’re getting a stripped down wunderlist, and when I say stripped, I mean stripped. Say hello to no notifications, no shareable links, no tagging, no calendar sync, no useable web version, no bells, no whistles, no, no, no.

“Hey but does it have collabora...” no.
“But does it have google assistant integrat...” no.
“Ah but does it hav...” no.

What it does have is simple tasks & sub tasks, with due dates. Like a list your mom used to write on the table with a pencil.

If you’re reading this Google, ship these features to make tasks 1000x better:

1. Add shareable links (no login required)
2. Add tagging
3. Make a useable web ui.

All that said, it’s kind of refreshing to use such a simple app. You know how to use it immediately out of the box without even thinking. Come to think of it, I’ve created 3 lists within the last hour & haven’t thought twice about whether I was doing it “correctly” or not.

No features to get lost in which is nice. Does a simple thing & does it well. 5 stars.

2.  Que al calificar las tareas como realizadas, en la sección de “completadas”  quedaran las subtareas dentro de las tareas para poder llevar un seguimiento ordenado de las actividades.

De antemano, muchas gracias

title: Chybí detaily
body: Tato aplikace je velmi jednoduchá a přehledná, což je za mě velké plus. Prostředí aplikace je přehledné, dobré. Chybí mi možnost například sdílet úkol, nastavit si oznámení na úkol – aplikace sice žádá o povolení posílat oznámení, ale nic nepošle; nastavit si prioritu úkolů, a také počet splněných/nesplněných úkolů, ať už procentuálně, či normálně. Za další by bylo fajn zajistit, aby v nastavení šel zvětšit font písma, což není úplně nutné, protože velikost písma jde zvětšit pro jednotlivé aplikace v nastavení. Když v Googlu využijete další nástroje, máte kompletní CRM i projektové řízení. Já platím jen Disk. Používám Gmail, úkoly, kalendář, gant vzorce, adresáře s dokumenty a Google Keep. 
Navíc gmail má jednu z nejlepších ochran.  
Jen musíte mít již nějaké zkušenosti a vědět co a jak chcete. To Vás žádná aplikace nenaučí.

title: Cleanes Design mit einem massiven Problem
body: zuerst einmal muss ich sagen, mir gefällt das Cleane Design dieser App. Genau auf den Punkt, und genau das, was man braucht. Aber was die App für mich unbrauchbar macht, ist die Tatsache, dass nach einer gewissen Zeit die keine Hinweise mehr gibt. Ich habe noch nicht herausgefunden, warum. Die App wird scheinbar beendet oder in Ruhezustand versetzt. Wenn man sie nicht alle paar Tage öffnet, macht sie nichts mehr. Blöd, wenn man Aufgaben eingegeben hat, und diese aber gar nicht angezeigt bekommt. Auf meinem iPhone 16 Pro Max sind die Einstellungen richtig gesetzt meiner Meinung nach. Kein Energiesparen, keine Hintergrunddienste beendet. ich habe jetzt deswegen schon einige Dinge vergessen. Das ist ja nicht Sinn der Sache einer Aufgaben App. Mittlerweile nutze ich von Google wieder die Kalender App, und trage dort meine Aufgaben Termine ein, denn mit Google Kalender funktioniert die Benachrichtigungen.

title: Potential vorhanden, ABER
body:
Google Tasks sollte man unbedingt in Kombination mit Keep/Notizen betrachten!

Also harte Aufgaben und Erinnerungen an Mails in Tasks, dann erscheint das auch sehr schön im Kalender „wie ein kurzer Termin“ und in Google Notizen (früher Keep) dann weiche Aufgaben, Pack- oder Einkaufslisten die gemeinsam abgearbeitet werden sollen, was dann auch Labels, Suche, ortsbasierte Erinnerungen,… ermöglicht

Vorteile:
+ gute Integration neben Mails UND vorallem im Kalender
+ Unteraufgaben mit eigenem Datum
+ Notizfeld für jede Aufgabe
+ E-Mail Verknüpfung von Google Mail sowohl im Browser wie auch in den mobilen Apps unterstützt
+ ohne Mehrkosten

Nachteile:
- wiederholende Aufgaben werden nach Erledigung nicht sofort mit neuem Termin erstellt, was die Planung erschwert
- erledigt man eine Hauptaufgabe, dann werden auch Unteraufgaben abgehakt, soweit ok, aber in den erledigten Aufgaben werden sie dann unübersichtlich zu Hauptaufgaben
- Unteraufgaben können nicht eingeklappt werden
- bei der Sortierung nach Datum werden die Unteraufgaben vorübergehend von der Hauptaufgabe getrennt
- geteilte Aufgaben sind scheinbar nur über einen geteilten Gruppen-Chat-Bereich möglich und in Tasks sieht man dann nur die Aufgaben die einem persönlich zugewiesen wurden, mal eben eine Einkaufsliste teilen geht bei Google somit nur über Keep/Notizen
- keine Ortsbasierten Erinnerungen, wie bei Keep/Notizen
- keine Filter/Suche und auch keine Labels, Tags o.ä. um Listenübergreifend Aufgaben darzustellen
- kein Export
- kein Kopieren von Aufgaben oder ganzen Listen
- mehrere Listen sehr unübersichtlich in der Verwaltung 

Fazit: ToDoIst kann gegen kleine Bezahlung deutlich mehr, selbst Microsoft ToDo bekommt das kostenlos in Summe besser hin… also bitte weiter an Tasks arbeiten!!!

ABER: man kann die To-Do Listen nicht mit anderen teilen. Dafür gibt es zwei Sterne Abzug! Google das könnt ihr besser!!!

title: One of the best, but Siri shortcut missing
body: I like the clean, easy and functional UI. Even though reminders catchend up, somehow google tasks is more pleasant. But I would really love a Siri shortcut to use for easy spoken entry of tasks. Then it will definitely be five star.
author: Olli221

title: Mäßiger Support
body:
Ich bin Fan der Arveit von Google und möchte eigentlich auch in diesem Ökosystem bleiben, jedoch verglichen mit der Microsoft ToDo App gibt es hier noch eiiinige Baustellen.

Potenzial hat die App allemal und sie hat Kernfunktionen, due funktionieren, aber eine Tages- und Wochenansicht bzw "geplant" Ansicht ist essentiell bei ToDo Apps, das wäre echt angebracht.

Problem ist nur, dass ich nicht einschätzen kann, wie sehr Google hinter diesem Projekt steht, weshalb ich momentan nur flüchtig die Entwicklung der App verfolge und sie nicht aktiv nutze

Anders ausgedrückt, entwickeln sie die App doch bitte einfach so weiter, wie die bereits bestehenden Apps, wie beispielsweise: Drive, dann erhalten Sie auch vier beziehungsweise fünf Sterne für auch diese App.

title: OK but needs easy improvements
body:
1) Not possible to fold subtasks under main task. Also, only possible to add one layer under the main task.
2) Adding a date and time is good but barely usable when not possible to add time interval! Adding time slot 'from' and 'to' should be a possibility.
3) Adding a date and time adds a reminder in the calendar view but not in the google calender as such. It adds in a task the task calender which can be viewed in the calendar. If you view your Google calendar in another application this is not viewable which makes it not very useful.

title: Subs tasks
body:
Al momento de colocar subs tasks estas luego de ser creadas se colocan en tasks que no tienen fechas. Propongo que al momento de crear una subs tasks te permita crear una fecha individual para la subs tasks! 

Ejemplo: si estoy haciendo un papel para un periódico y el task se llama “Papel para el (30/01/2021)” y de subs task poner “Hacer introducción - 10/01/2021”, otra, “Hacer desarrollo 15/01/2021), y así sucesivamente. Fuera mucho más organizado y permitiera que estas substasks tuvieran un recordatorio!

Supongo que Google irá mejorando y añadiendo estas cosas con el tiempo, o quizás discontinúen la app antes de añadirlas...quien sabe, Google tiene mucha experiencia tirando aplicaciones a la papelera y dejando a sus usuarios colgados.

En cualquier caso, celebro la aparición de esta app y espero que siga evolucionando, desde luego que Google tiene los recursos necesarios para que esto ocurra.

title: Pros: Free, works with Google Calendar. Cons: Everything else
body:
If you use Google calendar, and want a free, bare-bones To-Do List app that will show up on said calendar - this is that, and almost only that.

If you need a well-designed task app, that does anything else other than that: flee. 

Leaving aside that Google is the Internet equivalent of an all-seeing, all-knowing, amoral God, moonlighting as a giant billboard: 

• No search function (this is Google we’re talking about.)
• Recurring tasks completely disappear from the app if they are not currently due, so you can’t look ahead to see what recurring tasks you have coming up - though you can find them individually by searching in Google Calendar. Why Google Calendar has a search function that works on Tasks, while Tasks doesn’t, is beyond me
• Tasks can only have one set of subtasks - which cannot be hidden
• Longer Task notes get visually truncated, so you can’t see past a certain point
• No tags or hierarchical sorting
• Can’t rearrange the order of your Lists in the app, you have to do it via the web app
• Un-deletable ‘default’ list - as such, I recommend not using it 
• Recently added feature of “Due Dates” don’t seem to provide any sort of visual feedback in the app, not sure if they do in GC, also Due Dates are not editable in calendar despite being…dates
• I’m sure there was more…

Again, this is a Google app. A handful of small meaningful changes would put this squarely top of the heap, like most Google apps. But here we are.

title: duration of tasks
body:
I quickly found out every task is considered as a 30 minute time frame in your Google calendar. This is ridiculous because you can create lists with a date or time, but not a due date or specific duration. Duration for my purpose isn't important because events cover that, but making a task exactly 30 minutes makes it useless as a checklist for important deadlines. Reminders were better for that, but unfortunately you couldn't load it with more subtasks or details besides a time. It's awful google has you convert all your reminders into tasks without explaining this. I set a task for an assignment for a couple minutes before midnight so I have a list of due dates and so it would be on my schedule. Unfortunately on my schedule it has two parts for the end of day 1 and the start of day two for the remainder of the default 30 minute time frame. This is not a well thought out use for tasks and they are trying to replace a useful feature with something less useful. This is especially upsetting because they want to charge to allow businesses or professionals to have clients schedule directly ywoth their calendar, but you would have to use something different to create due dates. This will force users out of their walled garden. Apparently this hasn't changed in three years because there are posts talking about this 30 minute issue in 2020.

So my question is what I'm saying correct? Is there a fix coming down the pipeline, or has anyone come up with a proper productivity solution within google's systems (calendar/keep/tasks/etcetera)?

title: Still needs work!!
body:
For several years I was happily using another app integrated to Google tasks.  Sadly the developer didn’t update it to latest Google standards so I’ve had to swap to using native app.

My frustrations:
- Badge not working for me so I keep missing tasks.  Amazing how much the badge count reminds you after dismissing reminder.
- I used to have daily tasks like paying for car parking.  As my needs are a difficult pattern, the other app was so much better.  It would generate next task upon marking current one completed and I could then mark future tasks complete immediately ie buy 3 days of car parking, Mark 3 days complete. title: Ottima App, meglio di Apple promemoria, però…
body:
1.
La widget su iPhone dovrebbe poter mostrare i task da evadere in giornata, cosa possibile con promemoria di Apple. Purtroppo adesso è possibile visualizzare solo i task di una sola lista, il che rende il widget troppo limitato.

2.
Sarebbe molto interessante poter avere la stessa cosa su MacOS, per esempio l’app Scriptable può essere installata sia su iOS che su MacOS, in questo modo le widget fatte su mobile saranno disponibili anche su desktop.

Questi due suggerimenti renderebbero l’app di Google un pieno sostituto rispetto promemoria, anche perché il tutto è già integrato sul sistema Google, quindi Google Calendar e Gmail.

Basta migliorare l’esperienza utente delle widget, così da avere a primo acchito i task da evadere senza aprire Google Calendar.

Poi per il resto l’app è semplice e va dritta al punto.

title: Migliorabile ma così non va
body:
È una buona app ma sembra una versione monca della funzione similare di Google keep: Manca l'integrazione con l'app Google Calendar su iPhone; Manca la possibilità di aggiungere ed eliminare Task con Google Home; manca una versione web in cui gestire in modo più chiaro e meno sacrificato i vari Task, cosa che consente di fare, invece, Google Keep. Manca la possibilità di aggiungere immagini, cosa salvifica per ricordare i Task quando non si ha tempo di scrivere; manca un cestino in cui trovare i Task cancellati; e ancora: manca la suddivisione in giorni dei Task completati. Altra pecca è che se i Task con ripetizione quotidiana non vengono completati, dovrebbero comparire sia il giorno seguente che tra le "scadute" dei giorni precedenti.

Dopo mesi di utilizzo ho preferito tornare ad utilizzare solamente Keep che ritengo essere un sistema molto più completo e performante.

title: Deluso, ma “confido” in voi!
body: Sinceramente mi aspettavo di meglio da Google. Il design è ottimo e minimale. Ma... sembra di fare una l’ista della spesa, con le date accanto però. Dovreste aggiungere la possibilità di allegare documenti, il riconoscimento automatico della data (attraverso il testo), la possibilità di creare elenchi e tanto altro. Io preferisco Any.do o Todoist o Agenda. Questa non è una polemica (nonostante lo sembri), piuttosto una critica; perché capisco che creare un applicazione del genere con tutte quelle funzionalità non è facile (ma Todoist ed anche Agenda ci sono riuscite, quindi non vedo perché non dovrebbe riuscirci Google). Consiglio: meglio fare poco (realizzare poche applicazioni) ma fatto bene, piuttosto che tanto e fatto male.

title: Feature Request
body:
Creating tasks and completing them feels very satisfying.
I have a suggestion for improvement: it would be extremely helpful if tasks could also be visualized in a calendar view. In addition, having a clear due date or deadline feature would make the app even better.

Personally, I would love to gain a sense of achievement by seeing completed tasks visually reflected on a calendar. As an additional feature, it would be great if the app could notify users when a deadline is approaching, for example through color changes or alarms, which I believe would further increase user satisfaction.

I am already very satisfied with the app as it is, but I would be very happy to see these features added in future updates.

title: シンプルで最高！
body:
こんなアプリを待ってました！
もうかなり3年近く使い込んで、今ではNotionに次ぐ2番目に気に入ってるアプリといっても過言じゃない！

便利すぎて、今では
・やることリスト
・日記
・予定
・Gmailの通知
・アイデアメモ など
ToDoリストの幅を超えて大活躍です！

特にチェックを押すと完了が取れるから、GASで回しやすくて神！
・mailを見たら☑️
・アイデアが書き終わったら☑️
・今日の日記を書き終わったら☑️
みたいにしたら無駄なく、誤作動なく使えますからね！

あとはなんといってもウィジェットが神！
ぽんぽんぽんぽん小さいのをホーム画面に置きまくってるからもうパンパンになってるけど、直接アクセスできるのが神！　

そしてなんといっても軽いのが神！　高速で立ち上がってすぐにメモ、そして同期も早い！　


~要望~
・notesをスクロール時にキーボードが閉じてしまうのを治してほしい。不具合？　仕様？　これがあるから一般用の公式APIが提供されてないGoogleKeepを手放せない。

・書き込み表示のときにnotesのアイコン消せるようにしてほしい。これのせいで左端が少し削れる。どうせnotesの他にはdueしかないんだから境目はわかるだろうし、dueのみアイコンをつけるようにしてくれれば嬉しいです！

・タスクの一覧表示のときだけでなく、書き込み表示のときもURLを押せるようにしてほしいです。マークタウンで埋め込めるともっと最高！

・APIで.dueの時刻も取れる用になると最高！

・ここのレビューに書いても仕方ないけど、PCブラウザもこのアプリぐらい使いやすいものだと最高！　特にリストをチェックつける形式が最悪すぎる。だってタスクの直URLでも非表示だとひらけないんだよ！　かと言って全部出しとくのも邪魔だし、シンプルに押して開く用になればいいのに。

title: とても良かった。
body:
iPhone14で使用してます

気に入っているところ

 ◆タブ型である（iPhoneデフォルトのリマインダーと比較して、自分の好みはタブ型であるので）

 ◆フォルダ内で子タスク孫タスクが一覧で見られる 

 ◆子タスクのフォルダ移動が、子タスク内のフォルダ名をタップするだけなのでやりやすい

 ◆完了タスクが見やすい 

 ◆子タスクの並べ替えが容易で選択肢がある （選択肢：タスクを長押しするか、右下の・・・からか） もうひとつなところ （ただし重くなるなら、これらは不要。改善要望ではない） 

 ◆孫タスクに期限設定ができない 

◆孫タスクがあると日時の繰り返し設定ができない 

 ◆完了したタスクを右下の・・・から削除する際、全て削除されてしまい、個別に削除できない ◆リストの順序が入れ替えられない

先ほどから何度もレビュー訂正入れてるけど、全然改行が入らない…何か対立が⁈

ただ、リスト自体の順番入れ替えは現在不可。
これがあればもっといいアプリになると思います。

title: コレはダメでした。
body:
・iPhoneデフォルトのリマインダーには、写真を添付出来る→視覚的に『ぱっと見、一目でわかる』それが、Google todoには無い。文字ばかりのデータはアタシみたいな人間には合わないみたい。予定が漏れたわ。

・Google calendarはiPhoneデフォルトのcalendarと違い、日付に予定が表示される。
だが、このGoogle todoも表示されて、画面がくちゃくちゃに移行してゆく。ああこうやって画面が煩雑になり結局カオス状態になり、「完了すること」をほったらかしになる。無駄なタスクなんかもうメチャクチャ。アタシそんな賢く無いし。ならば、calendarでよくね？todo App要らなくね？って話。

・iPhoneデフォルトのリマインダーはcalendarとは独立した、言うなれば『別の時間軸で動いている』Google todoはそれがごっちゃ。ならばと思い、Microsoftのtodoを使用してるわ。これはiPhoneは元より、他OSのタブレットでも使えてるので、地味にされど『しっかりと重宝』してるわ。元はWunderlistでしたっけ？

・

title: つい無駄な動き😂💦もうやめたい！
body:
最近、物忘れがひどく、ついついやらなくてはいけないことを忘れてしまうことがたびたび😓。メモに書き出しても、そのメモをどこかにしまって、メモの意味がなく、やり忘れることしばしば💦。
そこで、このTodoリストに出会い、使いはじめてみました。ケータイは1日に何度も触るし見るし、このTodoリストを必ずチェックすることになり、お陰でついうっかりはなくなり、今までの無駄な動きは一切なし！むしろ、こんなことしたい、あれもできたらいいなと、前向きなTodoを入れるようになり、行動も気持ちも前向きになりました。
問題はいつまで続くか？ってそんな先の心配しないで、まずは日々、使ってみることを、実践しています。

title: あっちからもこっちからも見れたり、書けたりするのがいい。
body:
スマホからも、パソコンからも見れるから使いやすい。
フォルダ分けできるのはいいんだけど、
フォルダ分けすると、中身が見えなくなって忘れちゃいそうになるから、あまりフォルダ分けはしないようにしてる。
サブタスクが作れるので、できるだけフォルダ分けしないで、やることを書き出して、サブタスクに細かいところを書くようにしてる。
使い方は、
いろいろ日々思うことを、ぱっととりあえず書く。
後から、あ、こんなこと思ってたなって、やる事を整理する感じ。
途中書きでもそのまま残るし、あちこち時間とかアラームとか設定しないとオッケー保存できないようなものだと、結局描き途中とかできなくて、紙で書いたのにのこらないなんてあり得ない話で、そんなメモ書きみたいに使いたいためにはちょうどいい。
手帳を持ち出し用、デスク用なんかすると、どこに書いたかわからなくなるけど、これをつかうとそれもなくなる。
長い文章はメモ帳でスマホ、パソコンからみれるようにしてる。

title: 写真の追加&色分け 希望
body:
今まではiPhone標準のリマインダー(以下、リマインダー)を使っていましたが、Googleカレンダーと連携できるとのことでこちらを使い始めました。ですが...

1. 写真が追加できない
リマインダーでは、タスクに写真やスキャンした書類を添付できたのですが、こちらではできませんでした。このアプリからだけでいいので、追加・確認できるようにして頂きたいです。

2. 色分けできない
リマインダーでは、リストごとに色分けや、アイコンの設定が出来ましたが、こちらでは、アイコンの設定どころか、色分けもできず、少し見ずらいです。また、どのリストのどのタスクでも、Googleカレンダーでは全て同じ色で表示され、文字まで読まないと、なんのタスクなのかが判別できません。

以上の点を改善していただけると幸いです。

title: I feel this is a service for those who use it lightly.
body:
I use this service together with "Google calendar".

Its integration is very easy to see and I find it to be effective.

I also write down my daily ideas in Google Keep.

These services are very easy to read and use with peace of mind.

But in my opinion, when I make plans, I prioritize them. It's what this service calls a "list" feature. Not being able to reorder them is very stressful for me. I have to go back and rewrite everything on a blank page each time.

And the second thing that stresses me out is not being able to see the totality of what needs to be done. I want a page that gives me a bird's eye view of the whole thing. Otherwise, I'd be tempted to check it over and over again to see if I'm missing anything.

And I want warnings of things that need to be done urgently and importantly by color or otherwise. I don't want to look at this every day because I don't want to look at this every day, but I want to always be aware of deadlines.

This can be solved by showing it on your calendar in a nutshell, but for larger plans of a month or more is not suitable for I currently solve this problem by using a Gantt chart or some other auxiliary function.

I also have a lot of information in "Google Keep" for jotting down ideas, and it's never ending. It is not a clean state of affairs. When you make an appointment with this service, the corresponding information is in the library decimal system or as a shortcut. I would be happy to call them out. Maybe even labels, etc.

These are very complex and not beginner's attempts, but I'd like to give my opinion on the relationship between the services and I'm happy to do so. Thanks for the great service!

title: アプリ内の日付が勝手に戻る不具合
body:
他の方もなっているかはわかりませんが…
5月19日以降、ToDoリストが内容を変更しても閉じるたびに5月19日の内容に戻ってしまいます。更新すると治るのですが、別のアプリから内容をコピーして戻ると5月19日に戻っている...という状況になっています。
19日のまま更新せずにメモをするとそのメモが消えてしまったり、更新してタスクの内容を変更しても閉じてから開くと元に戻っていたり、面倒くさくてしょうがないです。
何より通知設定をしていたのに、この不具合が起きてからアプリの中が5月19日のままらしく、アプリを開いて更新したら期限が過ぎて通知がきた、という状況が起き非常に困っています。
ＷＥＢ会議など開始時間が不規則な状況が続く中この不具合はかなりストレスであり、今まで気に入って使わせていただいたのに非常に残念です。
早く治していただけると幸いです。

title: 痒いところが幾つか。
body:
シンプルなto doリストが欲しく、殆ど問題ないが幾つか不満があるのでレビューします。

日付順の並び替えがやりづらい。
基本to doリストは優先度で並べるものだと思います。同日の時間指定するほどではないが、優先度で並べたい時にいちいち手動で並べ替えて切り替える必要があるので非常に面倒。というか時間入れてみても作成順に並ぶのが×。せめて時間指定まで並べ替えの基準に入れてくれれば手動もちょっとは楽になるのに…。

サブタスクに時間指定を入れないと下にずらっと並ぶのがイヤ。
ただし欲しい人もいるのかもしれないので要不要を切り替えさせてほしい。
というかそもそもサブタスク完了時に項目から消さないでほしい。チェック入れてそのまま残しておいてほしいです。

基本はシンプルで満足してます。
改善されたら大変嬉しいです。

title: 気に入ってるけど、改善の余地あり
body:
紙のtodoみたいな感覚でつけられるものを探していたので、シンプルでいいと思います。
機能が多すぎても面倒なので。
考え方次第ですが、通知機能はあまりないのでリマインダーとしての使い方はできません。
良いところもあるけど、まだまだ発展途上という感じもします。
[純正リマインダーとの比較ですが、良い点]
・完了したタスクを一括削除できる
・詳細編集画面がタップしやすい
・タスク作る流れで期日や詳細が書ける
・サブタスク作れる
[改善してほしい点]
・期日が日にちだけでなく時間も指定できるといい
・空白タスクができるなどの細かいバグ
・せっかくgoogleなのだからドライブや他者との共有ができるようになってほしい
author: ウスイ

title: 個人的にはとてもいい！
body:
使い始めてから日は浅いですが、個人的にはとても便利です。
googleカレンダーを使用しているのですが、以前は違うToDoアプリを使用していたので、ToDoとカレンダーがどうしても分かれてしまい、漏れが多く大変でした。

ですが、これを使用することによりToDoとカレンダーが一覧できるようになり、とても助かっています。

ただ、一点だけどうしても使い勝手が悪いなと思うのは、タスクの繰り返し機能がないこと…。
毎月一回あるToDoを忘れないために、しっかり管理したいのですが、繰り返し機能がないので、毎月一回あるToDoに関しては、googleカレンダーの繰り返し機能を使用して忘れないようにしてます。
ただ、できればToDoの中で繰り返しができると、とてもスッキリします。

googleさん！お願いしますね…！

あ、あと、PC版のToDo管理画面が古臭くて少し嫌ですので、もう少しスマートでカッコい感じにしてくれると尚いいと思います！

title: シンプル……すぎるかも。
body:
他のToDoアプリに比べてデザインはシンプルで良かったのですが、機能が足りてないと思います。

いい点(変えないでほしい機能)
･シンプルなデザイン
･無駄にフォルダ分けなどが無いところ←フォルダ分けが無いアプリを探していたので気に入っています。
･自動で日付順に並べられるところ
･完了したタスクは自動的に畳まれるところ
･タスクに詳細を書き込めるところ←表示の大きさ、濃さも丁度いいです。

今後加えて欲しい機能
･今日やるべきタスクの数をバッジで表示←個人的に1番欲しい機能です。
･ウィジェットに今日やるべきタスクを表示
･繰り返しの予定を作成
･完了したタスクを一定期間ごとに削除←ユーザー側でON/OFFできて、何日後に消すかも設定できると助かります。
･Googleカレンダーと連携←カレンダー側では予定と区別がつくデザインで表示して欲しい、カレンダー側からチェックボックスで完了にできるとなお良しです。

title: Useful but slow
body:
It's good for noting stuff, with a clear interface and satisfying animations,

BUT it's painfully slow. It often lags by a few seconds and I never know why. It's so frustrating as if I remember I need to do something it can be in those seconds that I forget what I was trying to note down.

It would also help to allow subtasks to be given their own subtasks, as well as by grouping tasks by themes, and adding deadlines and notifications.

it would also be good to link that to Google calendar by reading your tasks lists and suggesting to create specific helpful events due to a Tasks entry

title: 미리 알림 대비 아주 좋음
body:
일단 미리알림은 강제 새로고침이 안됨. 그리고 일정 알림도 5분단위고, 할 일 합치면 맨날 튕김. 이것 때문에 Tasks로 옮겼는데 새로고침 아주 잘 됨. 일정 알림 1분단위이고 튕기는 일 한 번도 없었음. 

1. Apple Watch 앱 추가
2. 일정 한꺼번에 선택 (미리알림은 손가락 두개로 스크롤하면 됨)
3. 일정 삭제 버튼 밖으로 빼기 (• • • 한 번 누르고 들어가야함) 
4. 일정 목록 순서 바꿀 수 있게
5. ‘반복’ 설정한 일정이 그 날 이전에도 목록에 떠서 리마인드 할 수 있게

해준다면 더이상 바랄 게 없음. I ❤️ Google

title: 위젯, 구글캘린더앱 연동
body:
정말 다른 할 일관리앱과 비교하고 비교해도 그 기능만 보았을 땐 최고에요.  가독성도 좋고 나중에 입력해도 날짜순으로 정렬되어 바로바로 해야할 일과 앞으로 해야 할 일들을 한번에 볼 수 있어 이것만큼 마음에 드는 to do 앱이 없습니다. 

그런데 데스크탑용 구글캘린더에는 너무 완벽하게 연동되어 편리한데 왜 모바일구글캘린더는 연동기능을 지원해주지 않는건가요..? 심지어 미리알림도 연동이되는 구글캘린더앱인데 .. 어째서인가요  
위젯도 만들어주셨으면 좋겠습니다! 

많은사람들이 오래전부터 요청해왔던 단점인데 왜 개선이 안댈까요... 너무 아쉽고 간절합니다 ㅠㅠㅠ

title: Good but missing some very good features
body:
Great, easy to use, like all the features as they are so far. Google calendar integration is spot on. 

A few thoughts on useful additions:
- having a larger widget available 
- ability to have multiple widgets running at the same time showing different lists
- The ability to upload a photo, file or add a link to a onedrive file (for example) would be IMMENSELY useful. This would be a great feature, especially as a student, if i set a task to do smth study related, being able to link directly to the document or file or folder i need to work on would be so handy. Otherwise I leave the app and to go to the task and try find the folder and I easily get sidetracked along the way, 
- ability to repeat the task multiple times WITHIN the *same day*, not just daily. Eg repeating the task at 2 hr intervals. This would be useful for study, but I can imagine it would also be useful for people managing medication, for example. 
- One other cool integration would be with apple screen time. for example when a time based task pops up, activating a productivity or study mode, for example, would be amazing

title: Simple app but lacks a lot of features to make it a daily driver
body:
First off, this app is wonderful. I love how simple it is but Google needs to work on it more if they want users to come from other apps such as Todoist.

Even if they are only aiming for a simple todo app, they are lacking in a lot of functionality to make it a daily driver.

One example is the inefficient use of space in the iPad. If you don’t have one, the iPad app is literally just the iPhone app but in a bigger screen. As in, the button placement is the same, you don’t have a sidebar (you technically have but it’s not always present like it should on a screen as big as an iPad), and other stuff.

Also, it lacks other stuff you can expect from a digital todo list. For example: a lack of a “Today” tab.

This is so dead simple to implement and every todo app should have that tab. Otherwise, they are just a grocery list app.

Another example is the lack of collaboration. You can’t share a list with other people so say goodbye to using this as an app if you work with other people.

While I don’t expect this to be a project management app, it still frustrates me you can’t let your roommate or something access your grocery list. Or if you are doing a group project, you can’t let someone else see the queued tasks.

Lastly, I believe this app lacks the thing that makes people switch from other apps: Integration with the Google Ecosystem.

You can’t use it with Google Docs. If you want to remind yourself to edit this part of the paper, you’d have to go to the Reminders app itself to do so. If you want to see your Google Tasks on Google Calendar, you’d have to disable Reminders first. If you want to link it to a Google Keep note, tough luck. You can’t.

This app has so much potential. I really hope Google can give it the priority. If it does, it might just become the daily driver of millions of people.

title: Отлично, но…
body:
Приложение отличное, можно создавать свои разделы в них группы задач, а в группах - подгруппы задач.
Описание, дата, напоминание, отметка когда выполнена задача - прекрасно!

-Очень хочется видеть теги и поиск по тегам, либо ответственных(но возможно теги впишутся лучше всего)
-Когда отмечаешь задачу из подгруппы она теряется среди остального списка выполненных задач, а при раскрытии выполненной задачи из подгруппы отсутсвует фиксация к задаче которая к ней относилась. То есть приходится вспоминать к какой задаче относился этот подпункт, особенно если он выполнился в другой день от остальных подпунктов.
-Неудобно что подпункты нельзя свернуть, весь этот огромный список путается в глазах
-Редактирование цвета тоже пригодилось бы, хотя бы в 3-5 цветах, этого было бы более чем достаточно, чтобы скрасить визуальный вид списков

title: Исправьте, пожалуйста ❤️
body:
- Добавьте возможность группировать списки по разным группам. Неудобно планировать все сферы своей деятельности без группировки списков. Получается так, что мне нужно спланировать 3 сферы деятельности, а группа списков только одна. Получается так, что все сферы находятся в одной куче списков. Это очень неудобно.
- Также прошу добавить возможность менять цвет задачи в календаре в зависимости от списка и группы (если в обновлении будут добавлены группы списков). - Прошу добавить возможность отправлять списки в архив. А то получается так, что список больше не востребован и мешает, а удалять его не хочется, так как все выполненные задачи не сохранятся, и их потом не посмотреть во время ежегодного анализа своей деятельности, к примеру. 
- Прошу добавить возможность создания целей. Мы ведь все для того и планируем свою деятельность, чтобы двигаться к своим целям и отслеживать прогресс по выполненным задачам.
- Буду очень сильно благодарен, если мой отзыв будет услышан, а предложения рассмотрены, так как я очень хочу продолжать пользоваться вашим приложением. Спасибо.

title: The way I get things done from myself
body:
I am now an expert user of Google tasks. I get everything done with the help of this app. For each major area I set up a tasks list with an appropriate title, for example ‘Money Matters’ or ‘Bill Payments’. Then, tasks are created with the deadlines set.

I work independently; there is no boss. So, an extreme level of discipline is critical in everything I do. This app serves my ‘finger pointer’ that help me organize everything I have to do in one place. 

The app gets sync across all three digital devices I use. 

Google Tasks, Calendar, Drive and Google Meet represent my office, home, communication platform and all admin system. 

They all together create my the paperless virtual world that facilitate my ‘digital nomadic’ existence.

title: Please bring back the side menu/list selector in the Google Tasks iOS app.
body:
Please bring back the side menu/list selector in the Google Tasks iOS app.
I use multiple task lists, and the previous side menu made it very easy to see all my lists at once and quickly switch between them. In the current interface, the lists are displayed as horizontal tabs at the top, which requires repeatedly swiping left and right to find a specific list.
This is much less efficient, especially for users who have many lists. Please restore the option to open a menu showing all task lists vertically, or at least provide an alternative “All Lists” selector.
The previous interface was significantly faster and more practical for managing multiple lists. Thank you.

title: Please add basic iOS Shortcuts and Siri support to Google Tasks.
body:
The most important use case is quickly creating a new task without opening the app, navigating to the correct list, tapping “Create task,” and entering it manually.

It would be very useful to support:

* Creating a new task through Siri or an iOS Shortcut.
* Choosing the destination Google Tasks list.
* Assigning “Create new task” to the iPhone Action Button.
* Creating tasks by voice, for example: “Add ‘Buy groceries’ to my Personal list.”
* Asking Siri or a Shortcut to show or read today’s tasks.

The main goal is to make task capture almost instant, especially when using the phone one-handed or when typing is inconvenient.

title: Желаемые улучшения
body:
Добрый день. Хорошее приложение, которое позволяет держать все задачи под рукой: телефон, компьютер, ноутбук. В этом плане это очень здорово. 
Есть люди, которым также захочется поддержать небольшие улучшения:
1. Чек-лист в задачах. Это позволит делить слона на части
2. Поиск по задачам. По всем задачам, как завершенных, так и текущих
3. Вставлять картинки/скрины (для начала хотя бы это, не говоря о файлах (это потом 🙂))
4. Возможность создавать папки, в которых можно создавать задачи. К примеру папка «Работа» <- здесь будут рабочие задачи; «Досуг» <- здесь будут свои задачи. И так далее. 

На самом деле при внедрении таких возможностей, ваш продукт станет еще более востребованным и станет заменой любых других приложений подобного рода.

title: Good, not great
body:
Good: calendar integration, organization 
Bad: can’t toggle recurrence; can’t move recurring tasks between lists; can’t use recurrence for “gaps” (e.g. “mow every 7 day”, which is based on completion, not a fixed schedule. If I’m delayed 3 days due to rain, my next task needs to be 7 more days away, not just 4) 
Search seems pretty unreliable and is unavailable on the iPhone app. 
Neat: which Google scripting I was able to implement a “gap” solution that triggered off of a phrase in my title: “(repeat=7)”. Detects completion and Creates a new task 7 days out. Unfortunately (another ‘bad’), the task creation interface proudly disregards any “due time”, allowing the setting of only the “date”.

title: Longtime user frustrated by iOS version
body:
I’ve used Google Tasks for 10+ years, multiple times a day, with 30–40 lists containing everything from daily tasks to personal notes, memories, work information, and even detailed lists of what’s in my storage bins. It’s become an important personal reference system.

After switching from Android to iPhone about a year ago, I’ve been extremely frustrated by how limited the iOS version is compared with Android. And now, in the latest update, a particularly useful feature appears to have been removed: the drop-down menu in the upper-left corner that let you quickly see and select from all your lists.

With dozens of lists, having to scroll horizontally through them is significantly slower and more cumbersome. I genuinely don’t understand why such a basic and useful feature would be removed.

Please bring it back—and please give the iOS version the same functionality as Android. Longtime users like me depend on this app, and it’s frustrating to see it become less useful over time. I’m now being forced to look for something different. Ugg!

title: Please update your app!
body:
1) The Widget is borderline useless especially the square one. The rectangle one isn’t as bad. 

2) The UI is bad, old looking, lacks modern appeal. 

3) No badge support so you don’t know what’s due unless you use the widget or open the app. It goes in the Notification Center and that’s it. 

4) No logic for entry; “Do the laundry at 6 PM on Monday” will literally just write that out instead of adding those times. 

5) No voice integration with Siri like Microsoft ToDo and other Reminder/Tasks apps. 

6) No meaningful updates. It’s in maintenance mode. Look at the history and you’ll see nothing substantial for years!

title: Native Keep Reminders to Tasks kills functionality
body:
Because Keep reminders are now Tasks and only fire through Google Calendar or Tasks, I have to remember to open the Calendar or Tasks app so it syncs over after every new reminder is created. Otherwise, notifications will never fire or update properly
It also fails to pull the most recent edits of the note once created as a task - so if I add a last minute item to the top of the list later, it'll never update Tasks - even if I change the reminder time after it fires
If I don't open this app for a while (since I really only use Keep, not Tasks) - newly created reminders just never fire notifications
Very bad google , very bad…

title: Feature Request: Integrate Deadlines, Task Sorting, and Reliability Enhancements Across Google Calen
body:
Hi Google Calendar and Tasks Teams,

I’m writing to suggest a few key enhancements that would significantly improve my ability to plan, prioritize, and execute tasks using your tools. I rely heavily on both Google Calendar and Tasks to manage time-sensitive responsibilities, and a few key limitations are creating friction in my workflow:

⸻

1. Add Support for Distinct “Due Dates” and “Work Dates”

Right now, when I add a task, I can assign a date (and optionally a time), but I can’t distinguish between when I plan to work on the task and when it’s actually due. This causes confusion when priorities shift. For example:
	•	I may plan to work on a task Wednesday because it’s due Friday.
	•	If my Wednesday fills up unexpectedly, I need to know if I can push it—or if it’s a critical, non-negotiable deadline.

Feature request:
	•	Let me assign a due date and a scheduled work date to each task.
	•	Let me sort tasks by due date so I can instantly see what’s flexible vs. urgent.
	•	Ideally, provide reminders or visibility when a task’s due date is approaching, even if it’s scheduled for earlier.

⸻

2. Support Grouping and Filtering Tasks by Priority and Deadline

I use a variation of the Eisenhower Matrix to triage tasks:
	•	Important/Urgent
	•	Important/Not Urgent
	•	Urgent/Not Important
	•	Not Important/Not Urgent (these are often joy-giving but deprioritized)

To manage these buckets:
	•	I’d like to assign and filter by these labels or groupings.
	•	I should be able to toggle which task lists I’m viewing, similar to how you might show/hide series in an Excel chart.
	•	Whether this happens in Calendar or Tasks doesn’t matter—I just need one central, reliable location to group and interact with my priorities.

⸻

3. Address Calendar Task Input Errors

Lately, I’ve been experiencing a high failure rate when trying to input tasks directly in Google Calendar. The entries sometimes don’t save properly or disappear after entry. These errors are causing significant disruption, particularly when tasks are high-stakes or tied to hard deadlines.

Request:
	•	Please investigate and improve the reliability of task entry via Google Calendar.
	•	Consider offering confirmation messages or undo options when a task is created.

⸻

Summary of Needs:
	•	Distinction between due date and scheduled work date
	•	Sorting and filtering by deadline and custom groupings (e.g., Eisenhower Matrix)
	•	Toggle views for task lists
	•	Stability and reliability in Calendar task entry
	•	Integration and usability across both apps (Calendar and Tasks)

Thanks for all the work you do. These changes would be a game-changer for managing meaningful, time-sensitive, and joyful tasks alike.

title: Feature Suggestion Arrange Task by Preference
body:
First and foremost, I LOVE this app. 

That said, it’d be nice if we were able to rearrange tasks by personal preference once they have been assigned a date instead of arranging it by time. 

Some context:
 I brain dump everything that needs to be accomplished on any given day. 

I can end up with numerous random tasks for a day. 

Currently, the only way to organize is by time. 

Often, I assign a time to a task only to find another task further down that takes priority for that time slot. 

It’s a constant game of time changes. Up until I get the order right. 

It’d be easier if I could arrange each task in the order I want, THEN assign a time to each task as needed.

title: Better than others
body:
I tried two competing programs before this one, and neither could successfully do recurring tasks the way I needed them to. This program accomplishes this mostly without incident; occasionally a task appears in Google calendar twice for the same day. The solution is to open the task, change to a different day then back again, save changes, and presto issue is solved. I hope they fix that glitch soon. 

I would appreciate the ability to select different colors for different groups of tasks to make it easier to differentiate them in Google calendar; right now I need to identify the group in the task description which feels like a chore, but it’s workable. Performing complicated recurrence patterns requires jumping through some hoops but it is possible. I appreciate that all tasks can have a start and end date.

The tasks app attempts to show which tasks are for today, which honestly it shouldn’t even bother to do, as it doesn’t successfully convey that you have only completed one instance of a recurring task. Really this app and Google calendar should come bundled together into one product. I’m sure Google realizes this too. Hopefully they will combine them in the future.

title: Great, simple task manager
body:
I switched to this from Microsoft’s To Do and have not regretted it. It’s responsive and easy to add tasks. 

There are 4 things I’d like to see in a future update:
1. A search function. C’mon, you’re Google. Search is your thing, right?
2. For recurring tasks, when you mark one complete, it should immediately reappear with the next due date. Currently, it’s marked as completed and doesn’t show up again until it recurs. 
3. You should be able to move a recurring task to a different list. Not sure why it prevents you from doing that. 
4. Badges. Would be nice to have a count of incomplete tasks. Ideally, a choice in settings of all tasks, starred tasks, or tasks from a particular list. 

Thanks for the great, FREE app!

title: Good
body:
Google Tasks is very good and I find it simpler to use than Google Calendar, especially with the included widget for the iPhone home screen.

Pros: 

Unlike Calendar Reminders, Google Tasks that are not completed stay on top. 

Much simpler to use in Google Calendar than Calendar events. But you can still create a task with a specific time for an appointment which is nice. This is subjective because if you need more options with an appointment then you should go with Google Calendar.

The widget for iPhone is much nicer in my opinion than the Google Calendar widget. 

Cons: 

Can’t search Google Tasks. Why? This is such basic functionality for a task list that it really blows my mind that you can’t search your Tasks. If you have lots of tasks in various lists and quickly becomes unwieldily. 

Unlike calendar, Tasks can only use one color.

Summary:

All in all, I really like this app and I started using it in place of Google Calendar. If Google could just add a search feature, it would really improve this app exponentially

title: Great app but limited in what you can do
body:
It’s simple, easy and keeps you organized. BUT the app is limited with what users are able to do. 

 • Sharing- By now we should be able to share our list of tasks or individual tasks with other users. Yes, I know what Google Keep is. I don’t like Google Keep. The layout and user capabilities don’t have the same appeal. 

• Organization- More options for how users can organize individual tasks. Date, starred and recently added are not enough. 

• Notifications- Need more options or at least mimic the set up of ‘Appointments/ Events’ in Google Calendar. 

• Subtasks- The option to create an additional layer of subtasks under each current subtask. 

 I’ve tried other list keeping organizational apps, but I keep coming back to this one. I don’t have the patience or motivation to ‘learn’ another app. As a busy parent simplicity and ease are precious commodities. I’m sure if the developers made a few changes they would drastically improve the lives of millions of people. I’m talking Nobel Prize winning work.

title: It’s Fine For Day-to-Day Tasks, Not Planning
body:
I was really excited when I found this app. I already use Gmail, Google Docs and Sheets on a daily basis, but needed something specialized for task management. 

I want to say this is a solution, but it isn’t. 

Pros: It was easy to import and integrate existing tasks from Google Calendar.
The interface is really easy and simple to use, creating and managing tasks is straightforward.

Cons: Recurring/repeating tasks disappear after you mark them complete (even for tasks that are supposed to appear every weekday). They don’t show up within the following day, or even the current week. You also can’t add dates or times to subtasks. You have to open up Google Calendar to actually see your all of your recurring tasks properly.

If recurring tasks were visible and you could add dates/times to subtasks, this would be a five star app. In its current state, it is not viable as a task management tool and Google has received feedback on this lacking feature in forums since 2019.

title: Best for Personal Use
body:
This is a great, basic task app that works fine for personal use. However, I do not recommend this for businesses with Google Workspace/Spaces. Why promote this as a productivity tool for remote teams if basic functions and features of a shared task list are missing?

Not being able to sort, export, or print tasks from all lists created in Google Spaces via Workplace is a major deterrent and why I avoid using it if possible. I would also like to see the ability to add a status update and sort by status (in progress, not started, done, etc), plus the option to assign a priority level or even just color code tasks aside from the star option. And the most frustrating part by far - If you try to integrate using ITTT or Zapier, none of the tasks from Spaces will be funneled over, only those from your personal list. So even if you wanted to use a task app that offers the color coding or status features, you'd have to import the tasks from Spaces manually. You're killing me, Smalls!! *cries in VA*

title: Synchronizing task completion is awful
body:
Marking a task complete only truly happens upon opening the Tasks app. 

If a task is marked complete from a push notification, it doesn’t sync & show as having been completed across other devices or on Google Calendar…that task will still show as active. Only after opening the Tasks app will it then complete the task. This defeats the entire point of having the option to mark something complete from a notification.

Likewise, if a task is marked complete in Google Calendar, the phone app will still notify you that the task is overdue, & the notification of that task will remain on the phone until the Tasks app is opened…only then does it sync, finally marking the item as complete.

title: unpolished... waiting to be killed off?
body:
This is oddlly unpolished.

Multiple lists can be created, but they cannot be rearranged. It seems to be stuck on order of creation.

Single tasks can be moved from list to list, but not if it is recurring.

You can create sub-tasks, but they are listed as if they were tasks. There is an indent to indicate task/subtask, but it still fills up the entire screen (there is no way to "fold" sub tasks into the parent task).

Google, the company made famous and rich by letting people search for things, does not let you search for things in tasks.

There isn't an easy way to see tasks with due dates, unless you load it up on google calendar.

If you want a bare bones to-do list, there are worse options out there than google tasks.

Oh, and google killed the stand-alone web client for tasks. That's always a good sign...

title: Probably the Best
body:
This is probably the best reminders (task) app. Your reminders/to-dos end up right on your calendar. You can add new items via the widget, the tasks app, or the Google calendar app. 

A few suggestions. See if there is a way to verbally add to a list via Siri. This is something the To Do Microsoft app has figured out. 

Also, if I hold down on a specific time within my calendar I want the option to add a task rather than only choose from my different calendars, assuming I want to add an event. Maybe I want a task at that specific time and I don’t like that I have to click the plus symbol in the bottom right corner otherwise I can’t add the task. 

Also, I currently can share calendars with my wife. I would like her to also see my tasks added to the calendar/have viewing/editing access to my task list, but I get the feeling this is a private list she is unable to see since it technically is not a calendar. 

Second to last suggestion. Merge your reminders app into the task app. There is no need for both and the fact that task items don’t disappear from your list if you forget to do them or don’t end up having time, but reminders do… what’s the point of the reminds app then?

Final suggestion. DON’T discontinue this app like so many other Google apps. I’m getting close to the point that I’m done using Google products other than the most basic search, calendar, maps, and gmail because you’re proving that you can’t be trusted with how quickly you pull the plug and support on various products. I’m still really disappointed you essentially made google photos a paid service and there have been other apps or products I’ve been using and then all of a sudden I get an email out of nowhere letting me know you will be discontinuing a specific product on such and such a date. You may have more innovation than Apple and your search engine may blow Bing out of the water, but you need to stick by your products. Apple and Microsoft rarely walk away from products, so customers know if they invest in one of those platforms for software, it will be there for the long term. Just my 2 cents. So great product, I suggest those minor changes, and keep it around!!! Don’t make me regret pulling away from the other major list apps to give yours a try only to have you cut me off at the knees. I will have a hard time using anything other than your core if that happens again.

title: Mostly Great!
body:
I use this app pretty much everyday and I have for pretty much this whole year. Maybe a little more. It’s nice and simple. 

But as happens with any software that is good enough to get well acquainted with, you learn it’s quirks, plus I like to develop apps, so I’m extra aware.

Like I make a list for every day of the week, there’s not really a built in day feature. I have to move tasks between lists one at a time, both on the google calendars web panel version and the app version.

And there’s this weird thing where when you want to delete your completed tasks, there’s no way to clear all deleted, you have to delete them one at a time, and each time you delete one, it shows a snack bar that covers the bottom one. So you have to wait for the snackbar to go away in order to delete the last one because it’s covered up. That’s on the google calendars tasks web panel and the app.

You also can’t shrink tasks in the list to hide the sub tasks. It’s nice that you can have sub tasks, I use that all the time, but I don’t want to see all the sub tasks when I’m looking at a list of tasks. At least not all the time.

And finally, you can assign a time to a task so that it will show on your google calendar, only problem is you can’t set a duration like you can with any other thing on your google calendar, it always just shows as the same height.

It’s hitting me now that I didn’t really research any of the small complaints before writing this so hopefully I’m not speaking out of turn, but hopefully one of you developers sees this and takes the suggestions. Or y’all just hire me and I’ll work on them ;)

title: Good app, one thing to improve
body:
This is a great app, user interface is simple and elegant but with enough options to be highly functional.
Seems to me Google’s only major competitor is Apple/IOS.
Google does a better job here with allowing subtasks — that is very useful.
Two things iOS does better that Google should look into:
1. Location-based reminders — ie when I get close to Target, reminders for what I need to get pop up on my phone. AnyList does this (and is compatible with Google assistant) but adding this into the Google platform would be a game-changer for me.
2. Color coding lists — not a big deal, but would add to the aesthetics that Google is already so good with in its calendar.

title: Good start
body:
Very little functionality. I am surprised this is 4 years old and still looks like a first draft/early release. 
Cons: 
- Can’t collapse task with dependents
- Cant swipe to delete/add to task parent/add date. Only to complete a task
- Can’t rearrange the order of items entered
- No #tagging
- No color coding 

These were basic functionality I was looking for. One list for all tasks - parent headers with sub task that can be easily rearranged, drag and drop to dates based on availability, and to apply importance level. Fast quick actions to move with me in my busy day. I would also love to see the daily weather for a week at a time that I am planning for to now where I have availability  for outdoor tasks.

title: Too Disorganized in Date Mode
body:
I downloaded this app thinking, finally, a simple and clean UI that lets me create subtasks with due dates and room for notes. The bad part is when switching to view your list via Due Date. Say you have a sub task with its own due date. It will get separated from the main task and when clicking on it, have no ties to the main task. An example would be having a main task with a client’s name. And the sub task that says “send invoice”. When clicking on the sub task, there’s no indication to who the client is because it doesn’t link to the primary task. So if you have multiple subtasks that say “send invoice”, you wouldn’t know who it’s referring to.

I’m back on Trello and it’s much easier. It’s a bummer because I love Google products but this one isn’t there yet.

title: Great for quick use, but pretty limited capabilities.
body: I use this app to list urgent tasks (whereas I use Google Keep to log tasks that aren’t necessarily timely). I like that it is simple and straightforward for this purpose; I can quickly add and cross off new tasks. It is a bit cumbersome at times. I liked the idea that I could add sub-tasks, but you can’t check then off if you are clicked on the master task in edit mode; you can only delete the sub-task entirely or complete the master task, but makes the sub-task capability kind of pointless. Thus, I stopped using sub-tasks. My feed is now very full and unorganized, which is a bummer. One other complaint is that you can’t add a voice memo like you can on Keep. I do think this app has a lot of potential, though, and Google does a good job of making reasonable updates without too much time passing by, in my opinion. I assume it will be adjusted to fit these criteria in the bear future.

title: Nice app but need improvements to make it better
body:
First, thanks for allowing users to build up unlimited subtasks, set reminder, and create list for free. I really like the feeling of easy to drop down things. It relieves my stress. The app has already given me great experiences that in other todo apps, it’s only possible for those who spend great deal of money to subscribe. In other words, it’s a great app with potential that developers can dig into it further to create the best version of todo app.

From my using experience, I would suggest the following improvements:

1. Please also allow access Google task on Google calendars on mobile app. By allow access, I am indicating that by setting up the tasks on Google Tasks, I can not only see my task present on Google Calendar but also change time or edit the task on GCalendar. 
The reason why I so focus on this feature is that to make an effective and doable todo list, I need to cooperate with my other events and see how much time I can do sth from GCalender’s daily timeline feature to set realistic goals. So please do add it! It’s the most valuable feature!!! I 

2. About the subtasks feature, I would highly recommend that you guys can allow it mark under its main task instead of becoming an independent task when deleting the subtask.

3. I am aware that on the Google task, there is one list users can’t delete. I think you guys can make that list as today’s list which means that the app can automatically sort out what the user has set for today. By adding that feature, it should also allow users to move tasks from different lists to the today’s list. By moving tasks, I am suggesting that instead of adding feature in the detail of each task to choose add to Today’s list, the app should allow users to drag and pull the task among different lists freely. 

Look forward to using the update version!

title: Missing key features
body:
I really wanted to bring my reminders and to-do lists into the Google ecosystem, but Google Tasks is missing some key basic features. 

1. After completing them for the first time, recurring tasks do not show up again until they are due. This makes it impossible to look ahead at what you need to do until it is too late.

2. The app has no badges to display on the home screen. This makes it difficult to know if you have something overdue. Too often had the initial notification for a due task failed to grab my attention and then I am stuck never knowing that I’m supposed to do something.

I really tried to make Google Tasks fit my workflow for months, but I am switching to an alternative until Tasks is updated with these features. If that ever happens, that is.

title: I like it, but missing basic features.
body:
I just switched from Any.do because I got sick of paying for something I wasn’t using that much anymore. I understand this is free, but since google wants us to live in their ecosystem it could use a couple features. 

When I manually converted everything over I was happy with how the subtasks work. I’m using some categories for storing information and others are for tasks and tasks with due dates. There are a couple basic features that Google Tasks as a whole is missing regardless of platform.

1. No all task view or day at glance view. I don’t like having to go from category to category to see what there is to do today from my phone. It would be nice if they went over to the calendar on mobile like it does on desktop, but a calendar can already be pretty busy. The people that can benefit from an app like this the most probably spend more time mobile than they do in front of a computer. 

An all task view at least contained to the app would help alleviate this issue. I know I could put the stuff with dates in the calendar, but it requires way too much management for daily tasks that are really just checking a box or tasks that need to get done sometime in the near future. 

2. There is no order to the task lists other than when you add them. You can rearrange the tasks within a list, so why can’t I reorder the lists or at least have them default to alphabetical sort so they are easy to find. I noticed this after adding a few lists. I tried to think of every possible list I could need so that they are sorted alphabetically from the beginning. I can’t wait until I think of a new list that I want so I’ll have to rename and recategorize everything.

Also, Tasks should be accessible via the sidebar (like gmail) in all G Suite applications I.e Sheets, Docs, Slides. title: some missing features
body:
I really love this app. I have tried countless apps but I tried this one and have found it very helpful to connect it to my google account & calendar. I love the interface and the separate lists. However, there are some features that are missing compared to other apps that might force me to go back to another app until it is updated. 
1. No “snooze”
I have a reminder to take a medication once a week, and since it’s an injection, I cannot always take it right when I get the reminder. I don’t know when I will be able to actually do it, so it is hard to know a specific time. I wish that either, you could “snooze” the reminder or “remind me later/in one hour” (or something similar) so I can get another notification later on. Or, if I could set multiple reminders for each task. 
Plus, for my other meds, I would love to set different times for each day because I need to take them in the morning, but I sleep in on the weekends so I wish I could just have separate times instead of two separate tasks. 
2. An “all tasks” page
I wish I could see all of my tasks on one page. Having the different lists is great for organization. However, I tend to separate lists by different classes I take, and it would be nice to be able to see everything I have to do. Or, to have a color / label system so I could have a list with all of my homework, and then just color coordinate it. 
3. Subtasks 
This is a small thing, but it is a little inconvenient to not be able to have subtasks until you create the task and then edit it. I thought that there weren’t subtasks capabilities for the longest time until I decided to edit one. It would make the experiences much simpler to be able to add subtasks when creating the task. 

Overall, I really love the app and it has great potential! However, some features are limiting my productivity so I may need to use a different program until this one is updated.

title: Beware if you use repeating tasks!
body:
Update 4/4/2019: i’m going to revise my review and rating based on the developers response to my original review. According to the developer, repeating tasks will reappear in the list on the date that they’re due. I haven’t tested this yet, but if it works, it’ll make this app much more useful and worth a couple more stars. In my opinion, it would be better if the next task would appear immediately after completing a repeating task in the event you need to edit, reschedule or complete the next task before it’s due date. But, I appreciate the developer taking time to respond to me. 
——
If you set a task to repeat and complete it, it will not reappear in your tasks again until the day it’s due (according to the developer). So whenever you complete a repeating task, you will not be able to see it again in your task list until that day, unless you’re interested in seeing the completed task. The task will appear in your Google calendar, but only on the web-based calendar, not on the iOS app. Please note that you will not be able to edit the repeating frequency or date of those kinds of tasks until their due date. So it will be difficult to find future instances of your repeating tasks within the tasks app itself.

Also, as others have noted, the tasks reminders have no sound in iOS.

Besides the problem with repeating. I think tasks is a fairly solid application with great synchronization across all of your devices.

title: Simple and Fast, but Lacking a few Key features
body:
Great app. Already deleted all the other planner apps. Please take this feedback into consideration:

- Make switching between lists easier, such as a force press right or left swipe, or a tab menu (where the current "list title" is) that will display recently used 2-3 lists. 

- Allow the lists the communicate with one another. For example, users might want to move a task from one list to another (or simply add a task to multiple lists) and not have to manually insert it multiple times.

- Add a widget (this is a big one) so IOS users can access from home screen shortcut. 

- Under the Add Details, provide an option for users to predict how long each task will take (this would help tremendously for people trying to use a list as a daily planner and task list). 

If you take any or all of these suggestions into consideration it would be greatly appreciated.

title: Not Useful Yet
body:
The UI is decent and intuitive, but the app (as well as the web based Google Tasks) still lacks 4 incredibly basic but critical functionalities:

1. Needs to have a multi-task editing (aka  “bulk editing”).   I.e. the user can select several tasks and perform the same edit to them (e.g. change due date, change Priority, move to a different list, etc). 

2. Needs the ability to add notes/updates to a task (e.g. for a task to “Call John,” can add note “left voicemail on date xx/xx/xxxx.”

3. Needs landscape format for iPad use. 

4. Needs recurring tasks. 

If all you need is a simple to-do List, google tasks might be a great fit for you But for those of us who use Google as our business environment, we really need a better task app. I’ve shelled out a lot of money to try  dozens of them and they all end up being too complicated, quirky, or don’t meld well w Google.  Google Tasks has a rare opportunity to fill a much-needed niche, if they will make the task a little more sophisticated without going overboard into complexity.

title: Very bare-bone
body:
This is a very weak attempt by Google and I hope they improve upon that in the future.

The minimum requirement for a GTD app is the ability to set up recurring tasks, which is not supported by this app.

Furthermore time granularity isn’t any finer than a day. So you can not set up a task with a deadline/reminder for a particular hour in a day.

Web interface for this app is only available in the sidebar of Gmail, so anytime you want to access it on your PC, you need to open Gmail.

Since the new Gmail doesn’t seem to support reminders from Inbox yet, I’m under the impression that Google would like to divert setting up reminders to Tasks, but until they add support for recurring tasks and finer time-setting, Tasks wouldn’t be able to replace Inbox reminders.
